articles.title: Bukele deploys thousands of soldiers to Haiti
articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: El Salvador’s right-wing president, Nayib Bukele, announced on October 29, that he will deploy a military force of nearly 2,000 soldiers to Haiti. The Salvadoran president has justified the measure by citing the disappearance of four Salvadoran soldiers on October 18. The Salvadoran soldiers reportedly went missing following an armed attack in Croix-des-Bouquets, near the capital Port-au-Prince, involving the armored vehicle in which they were traveling. According to some reports , the attackers used very powerful weapons and explosives. Since then, the whereabouts of the soldiers remain unknown, and it is unclear whether they are still alive. articles.title: Final vote count for Israeli elections yields no clear winner
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: Israel’s Central Elections Committee (CEC) released the final vote count on Friday, October 30, confirming that neither major political coalition managed to reach the 61-seat majority threshold necessary to form a government in the 120-seat parliament (known as Knesset). The results show that the pro-Netanyahu bloc secured 53 seats, while the anti-Netanyahu bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot reached 48 seats. Meanwhile, Arab-led lists combined attained 19 seats, achieving an all-time high record in the history of Israel’s Knesset. The complete official results will be formally presented to Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday, November 4 once the CEC finalizes the review of any pending complaints or errors. articles.title: The Brazilian victory: left unity and digital autonomy
articles.author: Rezgar Akrawi
articles.content_excerpt: The leftist leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic victory in Brazil’s presidential election on October 25, 2026. The result came amid intense political and social polarization and the growing influence of the far right in Brazil and across Latin America, backed by the US far right led by Donald Trump. The significance of this electoral victory extends beyond Lula securing a fourth term. It also lies in the political and organizational experience that helped make it possible, above all the ability of diverse left-wing and progressive forces, with different programs and ideological outlooks, to forge a broad electoral alliance around common ground in confronting the far right. articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Large numbers of Sahrawi citizens took to the streets in El Aaiún , the largest city in Western Sahara, on Monday, to demand a just United Nations-sponsored solution that guarantees their right to freedom, self-determination, and independence. The demonstrations come as the United States allegedly pushes a draft UN Security Council resolution that would make Morocco’s autonomy plan the sole basis for negotiations over the future of the territory. The US-drafted text, reportedly circulated among Security Council members on October 22, has drawn strong objections from the Polisario Front, the Sahrawi independence movement, as well as human rights and solidarity organizations. articles.title: One year after the election killings, Tanzania still awaits justice
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: One year ago, Tanzanians went to the polls in an election followed by deadly protests and a violent security crackdown. The immediate unrest has since subsided, but the wounds remain, and the demand for justice continues. President Samia Suluhu Hassan was declared the winner with 97.66% of the vote, an overwhelming margin that came with the exclusion of opposition forces and mounting restrictions on political activities. The disputed election and the violence that followed exposed deep tensions over Tanzania’s political realities, democratic participation, and the state’s response to dissent. A year on, not a single official has been held responsible, and justice for the victims and their families remains out of reach.
